tests.title: fail closed: no actor, no patients; a portal actor has none either
scope by role: direct support own caseload, supervisor the staff they manage, clinician and administrator everyone
units: the flag is the rules-table threshold (75% used) and nothing else; 0 left is out
filters: attention chips, search by Lauris number, units flagged, staff, due overdue; counts match the rows
sorting: default is attention (red first); patient, units and staff sorts are stable and reversible
direct support: one h1, no paragraphs, only own patients, items under the patient with a verb, units bar with the flag, no console errors
expand and collapse: per-row chevron, Expand all / Collapse all, the choice lands in the address
supervisor: roster for their staff, Staff filter, chips filter the table, search by Lauris number, a patient opens the chart
filter state survives a reload and Clear filters resets it; an empty result says so with a way out
clinician: all patients, Responsible column, authorization chip with the unit bar, sort by Patient, items open their screen
administrator: statuses and dates only, no write or review verbs, no note text, items open the chart when the role cannot open the target
two-person confirmations: after the administrator proposes a designation the clinician sees the strip with a Review button; the proposer does not, and no strip when nothing waits
phone width: no horizontal scroll, patients become cards, buttons are 44 px
the old My Work, Do next and Staff dashboard routes land on the Dashboard; the review sections land on Documentation
selector fails closed: no actor, a portal actor, an unknown id, and a patient outside the role's scope all return null
the chart holds documentation with or without an authorization: T.W. has forms and no authorization; M.R. has both
clinician: header, Documentation tab with open items first, Open / All and Notes / Forms filters, sample-data chip on forms, tab to Authorization
a patient with no authorization says so in one line; the chart still shows intake, CNA and plan
supervisor: Review buttons for notes waiting on them go to the Documentation queue with the note; no write verbs
direct support: Write note on what is behind, own patient only; another person's patient is denied and shows nothing of theirs
administrator: statuses only, Open case allowed, no Review or Write buttons
phone width: the chart has no horizontal scroll and the documentation rows stack with 44 px buttons
roles: a raise needs a second person (not the proposer, an administrator or a clinician); a lowering applies at once; never your own
people: new users start as direct support or supervisor; clinician and administrator go through a role change
designated access: proposed by an administrator, confirmed by someone else, never for yourself, never a clinical-record grant for an administrator
rules: a reason is required, only the administrator edits, the type is kept, and a change is audited with its values
rules: the dependent screen changes (day-5 follow-up makes the Aetna request a follow-up call in My Work); reset restores it
units: the alternate bands change the units a day earns; restore returns the official bands (audited)
signature mode per document type: default remote (not validated); In person changes the rule the family screens read
family link questions: ask and required switches (the guardian link reads them); the insurance question is locked
the administrator has no clinical-record access: Settings never carries note text, and the matrix says so
Settings: seven tabs, one h1, every tab renders without console errors; only the administrator opens it
rules tab: filter by source, search, edit in the drawer (reason required, value type kept), history and the audit tab show it
units tab: the try-it box follows the bands; switching to the alternate asks why and is audited
roles tab: the matrix is drawn from permissions.js; designate in the UI, the clinician confirms from My Work, the grant takes effect
people tab: change a role with a reason (a lowering applies, a raise waits), the second person confirms in Settings or My Work
family tab: In person changes the rule, asks why, shows Policy not validated; the family-link question switches work
presenter tab: how it fits, architecture, maturity legend with all four levels, the unresolved decisions with where each is set
Login: four role cards, the family and school entries, no password, no demo chrome; signing in lands on the role's home; works at 390
